No notes yet.
Create a persistent note to keep checklists, meeting fragments, or debugging breadcrumbs alongside your project.
[New Note](command:saropaWorkspace.newNote)
viewsWelcome.scripts.contents:
No bundled scripts found.
Scripts are ready-to-run developer tools shipped with the extension, each with its own folder, run config, and declared tool requirements.
viewsWelcome.pins.contents:
No shortcuts yet.
Add a file as a shortcut from the editor title menu or the Explorer right-click menu, then single-click to open it or double-click to run it.
[Add the active file as a shortcut](command:saropaWorkspace.pinActiveFile)
viewsWelcome.recipes.contents:
No recipes detected.
Recipes are auto-detected shortcuts derived from your project (open on GitHub, run scripts, Saropa Suite tools). They appear here when this workspace has files like .git/config, package.json, or a Makefile.
viewsWelcome.watches.contents:
No watches yet.
Watch a folder for new files, a file for changes, or a GitHub repo for new issues and pull requests, and get a toast when something lands — even files written while this window was closed. New items since you last looked show as a count here and on the activity-bar icon.
[Watch a folder for new files](command:saropaWorkspace.watchFolder)
[Watch a GitHub repo](command:saropaWorkspace.watchGitHubRepo)

config.autoPins.patterns.description: Filenames or globs auto-added as shortcuts per project (removable). Removing an auto-shortcut keeps it removed.
config.doubleClickMs.description: Window in milliseconds for detecting a double-click on a shortcut. A second click within this window runs the file; a single click opens it.
config.previewMode.enabled.description: When on, single-clicking a shortcut file opens it in a transient Preview tab (italic title). Clicking another shortcut file reuses that tab, so clicking through several reference files does not flood the editor with tabs. Editing the file, or double-clicking a non-runnable shortcut, promotes the tab to permanent. Off by default: shortcuts open as permanent tabs.
config.showScheduleStatusBar.description: Show a status-bar item naming the next scheduled run and when it fires. Click it to open the last report, change the time, run it now, or turn the schedule off. Turning this off hides the indicator only; scheduled runs continue.
config.scheduleStatusBarLeadMinutes.desc: How many minutes before a scheduled run the status-bar indicator appears. Set to 0 to show the indicator only while a run is in progress or just completed. Set to 1440 (24 hours) to restore always-visible behavior.
config.defaultUseIntegratedTerminal.desc: Run shortcut scripts in the integrated terminal by default (so output is visible). When off, runs in the background and streams to an output channel.
config.terminalName.description: Base name for the integrated terminal opened for a shortcut's run.
config.interpreterDefaults.description: Default command prefix per file extension, used when a shortcut has no explicit command set. An explicit per-shortcut command always wins.
config.suggestions.enabled.description: Offer to add a file you open often as a shortcut. Counts are kept on this machine only and never transmitted. Each file is offered at most once.
config.suggestions.openThreshold.descrip: How many times a file must be opened before Saropa Workspace offers to add it as a shortcut. Re-focusing the same file within the debounce window below counts once, so this tracks distinct working sessions rather than tab flipping.
config.suggestions.debounceMinutes.descr: Cooldown, in minutes, between two counted opens of the same file. Re-focusing a file within this window (search, go to definition, tab flipping) is not counted again, so ordinary development does not push a file to the threshold. Set to 0 to count every activation.
config.suggestions.ignoreExtensions.desc: File extensions never suggested as shortcuts, e.g. ".dart" or ".log". Choosing "Ignore .ext" on a suggestion adds the extension here. Case-insensitive; a leading dot is optional.
config.suggestPinnedTab.enabled.descript: Offer to add a file to your Saropa shortcuts when you have kept its editor tab pinned (right-click tab, Pin) past the threshold below. Tracked on this machine only and never transmitted. Each file is offered at most once; choosing Don't ask again suppresses it permanently (restore with Restore Pinned-Tab Suggestions).
config.suggestPinnedTab.afterHours.descr: How many hours a native editor tab must stay pinned before Saropa Workspace offers to add it to your shortcuts. A tab pinned before this was tracked starts counting from when the window opened.
config.projectFiles.enabled.description: Show the Project Files view, listing files like README, CHANGELOG, and package manifests with their last-modified time and declared version.
config.recipes.enabled.description: Show auto-detected recipes (URL, run, command, and macro shortcuts derived from project files such as .git/config, package.json, and Makefile) in a Recipes group. Removing a recipe keeps it removed; restore them with Restore Recipes.
config.recommend.aggressive.description: Show the full menu on the Recommended shelf: lift the eight-row cap and feature every disabled scheduled ritual plus every recipe you have not adopted yet, not just the curated short list. Off by default, where the shelf stays a short, capped highlight.
config.configDir.description: Workspace-relative directory that holds the project shortcuts file (saropa-workspace.json). Defaults to .saropa. Change to .vscode to keep the pre-1.6 location, or any other dotted directory for monorepos where .saropa collides with a top-level package. Existing config is migrated automatically when this setting changes. Restart the window after changing.
config.defaultGroups.enabled.description: Show the built-in default groups (Build, Run, Deploy, Test, Docs, Data, Code) under Project Shortcuts, even when empty, and sort a newly added file into the matching group by its name and type (a 'publish' file into Deploy, a .md file into Docs). A promoted recipe also lands in its default group. Off hides the groups and stops auto-sorting; shortcuts already filed keep their group.
config.branchAware.enabled.description: Switch the active shortcut set automatically to follow the current git branch. Link a branch to a set with 'Link Current Branch to Shortcut Set...'; on checkout, the linked set becomes active (and its optional on-switch shortcut runs). Off by default; outside a git repository it has no effect.
config.aiContext.enabled.description: Scan the configured chat folders for active Claude/AI conversations and surface the most recent ones as shortcuts in an Active AI Threads group. Removing a thread keeps it removed; restore them with Restore Recipes.
config.aiContext.claudeChatFolders.descr: Workspace-relative folders scanned for Claude/AI chat transcripts (.md or .json). The 10 most recently modified files per scan are offered as shortcuts: a Markdown file opens locally (or deep-links to claude.ai when it carries a chat URL), a JSON file deep-links to claude.ai by its id. Each folder is scanned at its top level only, never recursively.
config.telemetry.enabled.description: Keep a local, on-device record of shortcut runs (manual and scheduled) to power the Recent group and the recents in Run Shortcut. Stored on this machine only and never transmitted. Turn off to stop collecting; use Reset Run History to clear it.
config.projectFiles.groups.description: Project Files catalog as a map of category to root-relative file paths (for example Project, Android, iOS, Web). A path may be nested, such as android/app/build.gradle; only the file name shows. Each file appears only when it exists, grouped under its category when more than one category has matches. Version is read from package.json, pubspec.yaml, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, and the top entry of CHANGELOG.md.
config.github.pollIntervalMinutes.descri: How often (in minutes) a GitHub repo watch checks its linked repository for new open issues and pull requests.
Sample your detected toolchain's processes on a timer while a workspace is open, appending a per-tool CPU/RAM/process-count row to reports/process-trend.csv and warning only when a tool crosses a RAM or helper-count ceiling. Off by default; the live monitor and snapshot work without it. Nothing is transmitted, and the heartbeat never ends a process.
config.processMonitor.heartbeat.interval: How often the toolchain heartbeat samples, in minutes (when enabled).
config.processMonitor.ramCeilingMB.descr: Per-tool working-set RAM ceiling, in megabytes. The heartbeat warns once when a tool (e.g. a leaked analysis server) exceeds it, and again only after it drops back under.
config.processMonitor.helperCountCeiling: Per-tool helper-process count ceiling. The heartbeat warns once when a tool (e.g. an editor helper swarm) exceeds it, and again only after it drops back under.
config.hygiene.mode.description: What the hygiene scan reports: empty (zero-byte files and zero-child folders), oversized (files and folders past the size ceilings), or both.
config.hygiene.fileMaxMB.description: Hygiene scan: a file larger than this many megabytes is reported as oversized.
config.hygiene.folderMaxMB.description: Hygiene scan: a folder whose recursive total exceeds this many megabytes is reported as oversized.
config.hygiene.fileMinMB.description: Hygiene scan: when greater than 0, a non-empty file smaller than this many megabytes is reported as under-size. 0 disables the floor check.
config.hygiene.respectGitignore.descript: Hygiene scan: read the project's top-level .gitignore and skip what it names (in addition to a built-in ignore set covering node_modules, .git, and build output). Turn off to scan ignored paths too.
config.hygiene.exclude.description: Hygiene scan: additional glob patterns to skip (matched against each entry's path relative to its scan root), e.g. "**/*.snap" or "coverage".
config.hygiene.bloat.folderCeilingMB.des: Workspace bloat scan: an immediate child directory whose recursive total exceeds this many megabytes is flagged as a crawl risk when it is not in files.watcherExclude. Default 1024 (1 GB).
config.hygiene.bloat.fileCountCeiling.de: Workspace bloat scan: an immediate child directory with more than this many files (recursive) is flagged as a crawl risk when it is not in files.watcherExclude. Default 50000.
config.hygiene.roots.description: Workspace bloat scan: extra parent folders (e.g. a src root holding sibling projects) to include in a cross-project morning sweep. Each child directory of a listed root is scanned as its own project. Empty (the default) scans only the open workspace folders. Findings in other projects are reported with their remediation; only the open workspace is guarded automatically.
config.displayNames.titleCase.descriptio: Show shortcut names in Title Case: strip the file extension, replace underscores and hyphens with spaces, and capitalize each word. For example, setup_arb_translate.py becomes Setup Arb Translate. Only affects shortcuts without a custom label.
command.openSettings.title: Open Settings
config.showRunToasts.description: Show a notification toast when a shortcut run starts. Turn off to rely on the output channel instead. Does not affect error, warning, or completion toasts from background runs.
config.sound.enabled.description: Play a short audio cue when a shortcut run starts or finishes. Off by default; the cue is additive to the on-screen toast and uses your OS's built-in system sounds (so it follows the OS volume and mute). The per-event toggles below choose which moments chime, and a shortcut's Configure Run can override this for that shortcut.
config.sound.onStart.description: When sound is enabled, play a cue when a run starts. Off by default (start cues can be chatty).
config.sound.onSuccess.description: When sound is enabled, play a distinct success cue when a run finishes successfully. Background and report runs report an outcome; terminal and external-window runs do not, so they cue only on start.
config.sound.onFailure.description: When sound is enabled, play a distinct failure cue when a run exits with an error.

command.releaseBoard.scan.title: Release Board: Scan
config.releaseBoard.enabled.description: Show the Release Board: scans the workspace folders' bugs, docs and plans documents and reports their state. On by default; turn it off to hide the status bar button and the commands.
command.releaseBoard.open.title: Release Board: Open
command.releaseBoard.openRules.title: Release Board: Open Rules File
command.releaseBoard.openSettings.title: Release Board: Settings
command.releaseBoard.projects.title: Release Board: Choose Projects
config.releaseBoard.projects.description: Folders the Release Board includes in addition to the folders open in the window, one absolute path each. The open folders are always included and listed first. Empty (the default) shows only the open folders. Set it from the Projects button on the board. This is a user setting: a workspace cannot change it. Each folder is read like a workspace folder, with its own .saropa/release-board.json when it has one.
config.releaseBoard.projectScope.descrip: Which projects the board shows once folders are chosen: all chosen projects, or only the open project. The chosen list is kept either way.
config.releaseBoard.projectScope.openOnl: Only the folders open in this window.
config.releaseBoard.projectScope.all: The open folders and every chosen project.
command.releaseBoard.previewGlob.title: Release Board: Preview a Rule Pattern
config.releaseBoard.reviewRequests.descr: Show the pull requests waiting for your review as a separate list on the Release Board. Uses your existing GitHub sign-in in VS Code, never asks you to sign in, and never changes a project's light.
config.releaseBoard.profile.description: What stops a release on the Release Board: Rush (extreme and critical), Deliberate (adds high), Zero defects (adds medium). A red folder always stops a release.
command.releaseBoard.mark.title: Release Board: Mark This Document
command.releaseBoard.exportMarks.title: Release Board: Export Marks to the Repository
config.releaseBoard.pathToGo.enabled.des: Show a Path to GO under each project on the Release Board: a short ordered list of what stands between the project and a green light. Click a project row to open it.
config.releaseBoard.pathToGo.maxSteps.de: Most steps listed in a Path to GO (3 to 20). Steps beyond the limit are counted, not listed.
config.releaseBoard.recipeEvidence.enabl: Let the Release Board read the newest daily report of the Build status, Test trend tracker and Dawn lint sweep recipes. A fresh failing report makes the project's row worse. A fresh clean report counts like any other fresh passing result. A missing or old report changes nothing. While on, missed reports of those recipes run one at a time at start, cheapest first.
config.releaseBoard.recipeEvidence.maxAg: A daily report older than this many hours (1 to 720) is not used as evidence; the row says how old it is.
config.releaseBoard.recipeEvidence.idleM: Minutes of quiet in the editor (0 to 60) before a heavy missed report, such as the full test run, starts at VS Code start. 0 starts it at once.
config.releaseBoard.recipeEvidence.rowNo: Show short notes on a project's row from the other daily reports: pull requests waiting for review, files not committed, a changelog or version mismatch, old unmerged branches, broken links and the release readiness summary. They are information only and never change a light.
config.releaseBoard.tidy.reports.descrip: List the tech-debt, merged-branch, workspace bloat and large-new-file reports as read-only entries in the Tidy box. The board only opens the report; it never changes or deletes anything.
config.releaseBoard.sinceLast.reports.de: Add one line to "Since you last looked" when a new standup digest or since-yesterday report was written. Read-only; it never changes a light.
config.recipes.staleBranchDays.descripti: Days without a commit before the Stale branch age recipe lists an unmerged local branch (1 to 365).
config.recipes.largeNewFileKB.descriptio: Size in kilobytes above which the Large new file watch recipe lists a file added in the last 7 days (10 to 1048576).
config.recipes.changelogFile.description: Changelog file, relative to the project folder, that the Changelog check recipe reads. A path outside the folder is ignored.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.enabled.d: Show a Hand to chat button on each release blocker, each Path to GO step and each Sittings step on the Release Board. It copies a ready prompt (the blocker, the file and the evidence) to the clipboard. Nothing is sent anywhere.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.detail.de: How much the copied prompt says. Short: the blocker and the file. Standard: adds the evidence. Full: adds what it waits on, its group, and the project's lint and test evidence.
After copying, offer to open the chats that touched the document, when Chat Explorer is installed. Never (default): only copy to the clipboard. Offer: show a message with an Open chats button.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.agent.des: The chat tool Hand to chat can open after it copies the prompt. The prompt is always on the clipboard; paste it into the chat. Set at user level only.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.agent.non: Only copy the prompt and show a message.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.agent.cla: The message gets an Open Claude Code button.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.agent.cop: The message gets an Open Copilot Chat button.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.agent.cur: The message gets an Open Cursor chat button.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.agent.cus: The message gets a button that runs the command in customCommand.
config.releaseBoard.handToChat.customCom: A VS Code command id to run after copying when the chat tool is Custom (for example workbench.action.chat.open). It is run without arguments; paste the prompt from the clipboard.
config.releaseBoard.keywordEditor.enable: Show the Edit keywords entry in the Release Board options menu and the Edit keywords and Restore defaults buttons on the board. The editor changes the phrases, threshold, weights and negation words that decide a document's severity, and shows which documents would change level before anything is saved. The note that your keywords are customized always shows.
config.releaseBoard.keywordEditor.previe: The most open documents the keyword editor reads to preview which ones would change level. A larger number is more complete and slower.
Open the chosen chat tool at once after copying, instead of waiting for the Open button. Off by default. Does nothing when the chat tool is None.
config.releaseBoard.pathToGo.showRunButt: Show the Run lint now and Run tests now buttons in a Path to GO. They start the shortcut the project names for that run, in the background. Turn off if the board should never start a run.
config.releaseBoard.overnight.enabled.de: Run each project's own lint and test shortcuts once a night, in the background, one project at a time, while VS Code is open and the window below is open. It records fresh evidence for the Release Board and never edits files. Off by default because it runs unattended.
Local time (24 hour, HH:MM) when the overnight window opens. A run starts at the first check inside the window.
config.releaseBoard.overnight.windowHour: How many hours the overnight window stays open (1 to 6). No new step starts after it closes.
config.releaseBoard.overnight.stepTimeou: Longest one lint or test run may take (5 to 120 minutes) before it is stopped and the next project starts.
config.releaseBoard.sittings.enabled.des: Show the "Steps I can do now" filter and list on the Release Board: choose the time you have and the devices and consoles you have in hand, and see one list of open steps across projects that you can do now. Nothing is hidden until you change a choice.
config.releaseBoard.sittings.defaultHave: Context ids switched on until you make a choice on the board, e.g. ["iphone", "mac"]. Empty by default: every context is then in hand, so no step is left out. After you change a choice on the board it is remembered on this machine. Ids come from the contexts in the needs dictionary.
config.releaseBoard.sittings.defaultTime: Time box used until you make a choice on the board: any, or steps that take at most 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour (60) or half a day (240).
config.releaseBoard.sittings.maxSteps.de: Most steps listed at once in the "Steps I can do now" list (5 to 100). The rest are counted on one line.
config.releaseBoard.future.enabled.descr: Show the Future tab on the Release Board whenever the project has deferred or blocked documents (plans/deferred, plans/blocked, docs/deferred, docs/blocked). The tab only lists them; it never counts as a problem and never changes a light.
config.releaseBoard.future.defaultSort.d: How items are ordered inside each flag on the Future tab until you choose another order on the tab.
config.releaseBoard.future.defaultSort.s: Wow and reach, divided by effort; lower risk first on a tie.
config.releaseBoard.future.researchParal: Most documents the Future tab hands to a chat at once with Hand all to chat (1 to 10). The rest stay queued and the button says how many remain; press it again for the next batch.
config.releaseBoard.inProgress.enabled.d: List documents you are editing in this window under "In progress" on the Release Board: open documents with unsaved edits or with changes in the git working tree that belong to the board. Documents marked in progress stay listed after them. Turn off to list only the documents marked in progress.
config.releaseBoard.inProgress.max.descr: Most documents listed under "In progress" (1 to 50). The rest are counted on one line.
config.releaseBoard.tidy.enabled.descrip: Show a "Ready to tidy" box on the Release Board: documents whose steps are all done and that have not changed for a while. The board only lists them; a document moves to the archive folder only after you click its button and confirm.
config.releaseBoard.tidy.afterDays.descr: Days a finished document must stay unchanged before it is listed as ready to tidy (1 to 365).
config.releaseBoard.tidy.archiveFolder.d: Folder, inside the project, that tidied documents move to. A dated sub-folder (year, month, day) is added. A path outside the project is ignored and the default is used.
config.releaseBoard.train.enabled.descri: Show a Release train row on the board and in the sidebar when more than one project is found. It groups the projects that ship together, shows one light (the worst of its projects) and the order to ship them in. It only reads; it never writes into a document.
config.releaseBoard.train.naming.descrip: How a release train is named: by the version of the project that ships last, or by its folder name.
config.releaseBoard.train.naming.version: The version from package.json or pubspec.yaml; the folder name when no version can be read.
config.releaseBoard.sittings.onlyOwnerDo: List only steps from your own checks: documents the rules file marks as owner action (the human folder by default; set ownerKinds or ownerFolders in .saropa/release-board.json to change that). Turn off to list steps from every open document.
Show, in the editor, which open Release Board documents name the current file. Needs the Release Board to be on. Reads the last board result and never starts a scan.
config.releaseBoard.editorLinks.codeLens: Show a line at the top of a file listing the open Release Board documents that name it. Click a name to open the document.
config.releaseBoard.editorLinks.statusBa: Show a status bar item with the number of open documents naming the current file, in the color of the worst one.
config.releaseBoard.editorLinks.minSever: Only show documents of at least this severity in the editor: any, medium, high or critical. Documents whose text was not read are left out when this is not any. Documents waiting on another document are collapsed on the board and never listed. Raise it if the editor lines feel noisy.
views.releaseBoard.name: Release Board
command.releaseBoard.overnight.enable.ti: Release Board: Turn On Overnight Proof
command.releaseBoard.overnight.dismissOf: Release Board: Hide the Overnight Proof Offer
config.releaseBoard.sidebar.enabled.desc: Show the Release Board at the top of the Saropa Workspace sidebar: one row per project with its light (NO-GO, UNVERIFIED or GO) and its first blockers. Needs the Release Board to be on. It reads the last result and a quiet background scan, and never opens a window.
config.releaseBoard.sidebar.blockersPerP: Most blockers listed under each project in the sidebar (0 to 10). 0 shows project rows only.
config.releaseBoard.sidebar.expandProjec: Which projects start open in the sidebar, showing their blockers.
Projects that are NO-GO start open.
config.releaseBoard.openOnStartup.descri: Open the Release Board as an editor tab when a window starts, in a group beside the active editor and without taking focus, and only once per window start. It is not opened again after you close it.
config.releaseBoard.openOnStartup.never: Never open the board at startup.
config.releaseBoard.openOnStartup.whenPr: Open it when the first scan finds open documents (red, amber or purple) in at least one project.
config.releaseBoard.openOnStartup.always: Open it whenever a folder is open.
config.releaseBoard.placement.descriptio: Where the Release Board tab opens. It is one tab: opening it again shows the existing tab where it is, and it remembers the group you moved it to for this workspace.
config.releaseBoard.placement.beside: Open it in its own editor group beside your files.
config.releaseBoard.placement.sameGroup: Open it in the same editor group as the active file.
config.releaseBoard.openBeside.descripti: Open documents from the Release Board in another editor group so they sit side by side with the board. Uses an existing other group, or opens one beside. Has no effect when the board is set to open in the same group as the active file.
Tint the Release Board status bar button with the worst light of all projects (red for NO-GO, amber for UNVERIFIED, green for GO) and name it in the tooltip.
viewsWelcome.releaseBoard.failed:
The scan failed, so there is nothing to show yet. Check the Saropa Release Board output.
[Retry](command:saropaWorkspace.releaseBoard.sidebar.refresh)
[Open the rules file](command:saropaWorkspace.releaseBoard.openRules)
config.releaseBoard.liveEvidence.enabled: Show a small flame on a Release Board row when the source files that document names have errors or warnings (from the Problems panel, the Saropa Lints file and, when installed, Log Capture). The mark is information only: it never changes a light.
config.releaseBoard.liveEvidence.include: Count warnings as well as errors and crashes. Off: a row is marked only for errors and crashes.
config.releaseBoard.liveEvidence.lookbac: How many days of debug runs Log Capture is asked about (1 to 30). Ignored when Log Capture is not installed.
config.releaseBoard.liveEvidence.unnamed: List crash signals from debug runs in files that no open document names, with a button that starts a bug document. Needs Log Capture; shows nothing without it.
Release Board: Mark Changes as Seen
config.releaseBoard.sinceLast.enabled.de: Show what changed on the Release Board since it was last seen: new blockers, cleared blockers and lights that moved. Shown at the top of the board, in the sidebar and in the status bar tooltip, and only when something changed. It clears itself after the board tab has been on screen for 8 seconds. Reads and compares only; it never changes a light and never writes into your documents.
Most document titles listed under each project in the "Since you last looked" strip (1 to 20). Further titles are counted on one line.
